Indian Standard ( Reaffirmed 1999 ) 

SPECIFICATION FOR 'O'-RINGS 

PART 2 MATERIAL SELECTION AND 
QUALITY ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA 



1. Scope — Covers the material, selection requirements, and quality acceptance criteria for 'O'-Rings 
for reciprocating and static purposes. 

2. Material — The eiastomeric compound used for the manufacture of 'O'-ring shall be of suitable 
grade satisfying the requirements of finished products. 

2.1 Guidelines for the selection of suitable eiastomeric compounds are given in Appendix A. However, 
this recommendation does not restrict the use of other compounds suitable for manufacturing 'O'-rings 
of required quality. 

3. Quality Acceptance Criteria 

3.1 Tests - Ail test procedures shall be as in the relevant parts of IS : 3400 'Methods of tests for 
vulcanized rubbers'. The tests shall be carried out from the finished products wherein practicable or 
from prepared test slabs of approximately same degree of vulcanization and using the same compounds. 

3.2 Workmanship and Finish - The surface of the 'O'-rings shall be smooth, free from air bubbles 
and other moulding defects. 

3.2.1 The various categories of surface imperfections on 'O'-rings are detailed below and the maxi- 
mum acceptable limits for surface imperfections on 'O'-rings are given in Table 1. 

a) Off register— Misaligned 'O'-ring halves caused by the lateral shift of one mould cavity 

plate relative to the other. 

ai) Mismatch — The cross sectional radius in one ring half unequal to that of the other half. 
It is caused by the dimensional differences in mould halves. 

b) Flash — A film like material, which extends from parting line projection in ID and OD. 
It is caused by the mould separation or inadequate trim. 

\ c) Backrind — A longitudinal recess of wide angle M /' or 'W tike cross sections oriented 
circumferentiaily and located at parting lines. 

c x ) Parting line indentation-— A shallow saucer like recess, sometimes triangular in shape, 
located on the parting line at ID and OD which is caused by deformation of mould edge at parting, 

lines. 

d) Excessive trimming — A flat and often roughened area around ID and/or OD of an 'O'-ring 

caused by the trimming process. 

e) Flow marks — A thread-like recess, usually curved, of very slight depth in the unflexed state 
with the normal surface texture and rounded edge. It is caused by incomplete flow and knit of the 
material. 

f) Non-refills, air pockets — A randomly spaced irregular shaped surface indentation having 
a coarser texture than the normal 'O'-ring surface or caused by the removal of foreign material. 

fi) Foreign material — Any extraneous embedded matter (contamination, dirt, etc). 

fa) Mould deposit indentation — Surface indentation, irregular in shape with rough surface texture 
caused by build up of hardened deposits adhering to the mould cavity.

IS:9975(Part2)-1984 

4. Marking 

4.1 The 'O'-rings shall be marked with the following: 

a) Manufacturer's name or trade-mark; 

b) Size code identification as in IS : 9975 (Part 1)-1981 'Specification for 'O'-rings: Parti 
Dimensions'. 

4.2 Certification Marking — Details available with the Bureau of Indian Standards. 

5. Sampling 

5.1 Lot — The 'O'-rings of same cross section and size code belonging to the same consignment shall 
constitute a lot. 

5.2 Unless otherwise agreed between the buyer and the seller, the 'O'-rings shall be selected from a 
lot at random for inspecting dimensions. To ensure the randomness of selection, procedure given in 
IS : 4905-1968 'Methods for random sampling' shall be followed. 

5.3 The sampling inspection plan shall conform to IS : 2500 ( Part 1)-1973 'Sampling and inspection 
tables: Part 1 Inspection by attributes and by count of defects (first revision)'. The specific sampling 
plan shall be as agreed to between the manufacturer and the purchaser. 

6. Other Requirements 

6.1 Dimensions — The dimensions of 'O'-rings shall be as given in IS : 9975 (Part 1)-1981. 

6.2 Seai Housing Dimensions, Tolerances and Design Criteria — shall be as given in IS : 9975 
(Part 3)-1 984 'Specification for 'O'-rings: Part 3 Seal housing dimensions and tolerances and 
design criteria for standard application', 

6.3 Terminology and Definitions of Terms — The terminology and definitions of terms used in this 
standard shall be as given in IS : 9975 (Part 4)-1984 'Specification for 'O'-rings: Part 4 Terminology 
and definitions of terms'. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

To obtain a reasonable life from 'O'-rings at high temperatures, the working conditions become 
of the greatest importance and it is strongly recommended that the users consult the manufacturer to 
ensure that all factors are considered and correct compound chosen. 

In formulating this standard due consideration has been given to the indigenous availability of 
raw materials and the need to cast the specification more on physical test basis rather than chemical 
tests. 

Considerable assistance has been derived from the following sources in preparation of this 
standard: 

a) IRSS/R61 -76— Indian Railway Standard Specification for moulded silicon rubber seals. 

b) IPSS/1-02-001/April 1975 — Interplant Standard — Steel Industry — Specification for 'O'-rings 

— Dimensional tolerances and guidelines for selection. 

c) ISO/3601 — Part Ml — Fluid Systems — 'O'-rings Quality Acceptance Criteria — International 

Organization for Standardization. 

The other standards in the series related to *0'-rings are: 

Part 1 Dimensions 

Part 3 Seal housing dimension and tolerances and design criteria for standard application 

Part 4 Terminology and definition of terms
